text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure) involves a combination of healthy lifestyle changes and, when needed, prescription medications.
snippet_highlighted_words: healthy lifestyle changes and, when needed, prescription medications

list.snippet: DASH Diet: Eat more fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while cutting back on saturated fats.
Reduce Sodium: Lower your daily salt intake to help reduce fluid retention and strain on blood vessels.
Exercise Regularly: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity, like brisk walking, each week.
Manage Weight: Lose extra weight and maintain a healthy body mass index (BMI).
Limit Alcohol and Quit Smoking: Reduce alcohol consumption and avoid tobacco to protect your heart and blood vessels.
Manage Stress: Practice relaxation techniques and get enough quality sleep.

text_blocks.snippet: When lifestyle changes are not enough—or for stage 2 hypertension—doctors commonly prescribe one or more of these first-line drug classes:

list.snippet: Thiazide Diuretics ("Water Pills"): Help your body get rid of excess sodium and water. You can learn more about how they work via the American Heart Association.
Calcium Channel Blockers: Prevent calcium from entering muscle cells in the heart and blood vessels to let them relax. Additional details are outlined by the National Institutes of Health.
ACE Inhibitors and ARBs: Relax blood vessels by blocking specific hormones that cause them to constrict. ARBs are often preferred if you develop a dry cough from ACE inhibitors.

text_blocks.snippet: Many patients require a combination of two or more low-dose blood pressure medications from different classes to reach their target goal (typically under 130/80 mmHg). You can review broader clinical protocols through the Mayo Clinic.
